newsitem.title: FRANCE: Bordeaux wine exports rise despite nuclear boycott.
newsitem.headline: Bordeaux wine exports rise despite nuclear boycott.

text.p: Exports of Bordeaux wines rose by 2 percent in volume and 13 percent in value during the 1995-1996 season despite the effects of a north European consumer boycott against French nuclear weapons tests.

The CIVB Bordeaux wine industry body said Wednesday that between Sept. 1, 1995 and Aug. 31, 1996, some 1.874 billion hectolitres (48.7 billion gallons) of wine had been exported with a value of 4.85 billion francs ($953.1 million).
Red Bordeaux wines were up 6 percent in volume and 16 percent in value while white wines registered a decline of 9 percent in volume and 3 percent in value.

The effects of the nuclear test boycott were most clearly felt in sales to north European countries, CIVB said. Exports to Norway fell 34 percent in volume, in Denmark they were down by 30 percent and in Sweden the plunge was 56 percent.
The CIVB said that the lost sales were compenstated by good exports to other European Union markets and sales rises in Switzerland and in particular Japan and south east Asia.
